evidence: Diff commit body: "reproduces on git 2.54, not 2.47" and "posture unit tests 13-fail on old code" — the concurrency signal is git-version-sensitive.
docs/adr/0051: "git-version-sensitive: reproduced reliably on git 2.54, never on git 2.47."

.github/workflows/test.yml:154-408 — the `test` job installs no specific git and no `apt-get install git`; search for `git-version` and `apt-get install` in .github returned no matches, so CI uses the runner default git.
tests/interfaces/store/_prune_race_worker.py drives real git subprocesses via init_repo; corruption only manifests when the stock git detaches maintenance.
advisory.finding: The re-enabled concurrency regression test only exhibits the corruption failure on git >= 2.47 (the commit/ADR state it reproduces on 2.54 and never on 2.47), but the CI test workflow neither pins nor installs a git version and relies on the runner's stock git. On a runner with an older git, the test passes regardless of whether the foreground-maintenance fix is present, so it cannot detect a regression that re-detaches maintenance — the core behavior this change fixes.
scenarios: A CI runner (or contributor) whose stock git is < 2.47 runs the integration tier green even if `maintenance.autoDetach=false` were reverted.
A future git behavior change that re-detaches maintenance silently escapes this regression test on older-git matrices.
advisory.suggested_fix: Gate the test with a git-version guard (e.g. skip-with-reason below the version that exhibits detached maintenance, or pin a git that does) and/or add an assertion on the effective maintenance posture, so the regression signal does not silently depend on the runner's stock git.
